```{r}
# Input parameters - fixed

n<- 28 # population size
ct.rates<-3 # avg number of daily contacts per day
nSeeds<-1 # number of cases starting the epidemic
R0<-2 # average number of secondary cases generated per infected individual in a fully susceptible population
t.stop  <- 360 # maximum number of days the simulation is running (if infected cases present)

# Compute the reproduction number related to the selected network. 
source("F:\\Statistics UHasselt\\Semester 4\\Master Thesis\\Master-Thesis---Chau-\\SEIR_contact-rates.R")
nSim<-1000
nSeed<-01042026
set.seed(nSeed)

# Define roles for all individuals 
roles_baseline <- rep("volunteer", n)
roles <- c(rep("vol", 24), rep("staff", 4))  

# Initialize result storage
baseline_results <- list() 
group_results <- list() 
strict_results <- list()

for (i in 1:nSim) {
  if (i %% 100 == 0) {
    cat("Simulation:", i, "/", nSim, "\n")}
  
  # SCENARIO 1: Free mixing (baseline)
  baseline_results[[i]] <- sim.epi_seir(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, nSeeds = nSeeds,  
    R0 = R0, t.stop = t.stop, roles = roles_baseline)
  
  # SCENARIO 2: Staff-Bridge - Volunteers in rooms + Staff moving between
  # IDs 1-12: Volunteers Group A | IDs 13-24: Volunteers Group B | IDs 25-28: Staff
  volunteers_a <- 12
  volunteers_b <- 12
  staff  <- 4
  
  scenario2 <- c(rep(1, volunteers_a), rep(2, volunteers_b), rep(3, staff))
  
  # Mixing Matrix (M) for 3 groups:
  # Rows = Infector Group, Cols = Potential Infectee Group
  # Probabilities should represent the likelihood of contact
  M_matrix <- matrix(c(
    0.90, 0.00, 0.10,  # Group 1 (Volunteers A) stays in Room A (90%), only sees Staff (10%)
    0.00, 0.90, 0.10,  # Group 2 (Volunteers B) stays in Room B (90%), only sees Staff (10%)
    0.40, 0.40, 0.20   # Group 3 (Staff) visits A (40%), B (40%), and other Staff (20%)
  ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)

  group_results[[i]] <- sim.epi_seir(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, nSeeds = nSeeds, 
    R0 = R0, t.stop = t.stop, roles = roles,
    group_assign = scenario2, M = M_matrix)

  # SCENARIO 3: Strict Cohorting - Staff A for Group A, Staff B for Group B
  # n=28: 12 Volunteers A, 12 Volunteers B, 2 Staff A, 2 Staff B
  volunteers_room <- 12
  staff_room <- 2
  
  # Group 1: Volunteers A | Group 2: Volunteers B | Group 3: Staff A | Group 4: Staff B
  scenario3 <- c(rep(1, volunteers_room), rep(2, volunteers_room), 
                     rep(3, staff_room), rep(4, staff_room))
  
  # Matrix M for 4 groups: Staff A (Group 3) only meets Volunteers A (Group 1). Staff B (Group 4) only meets Volunteers B (Group 2).
  # There is no overlap between Group (1,3) and Group (2,4).
  M_strict <- matrix(c(
    0.90, 0.00, 0.10, 0.00,  # Group 1 (Volunteers A) stays in Room A (90%), only sees Staff A (10%)
    0.00, 0.90, 0.00, 0.10,  # Group 2 (Volunteers B) stays in Room B (90%), only sees Staff B (10%)
    0.50, 0.00, 0.50, 0.00,  # Group 3 (Staff A) visits A (50%), and other Staff A (50%)
    0.00, 0.50, 0.00, 0.50   # Group 3 (Staff B) visits B (50%), and other Staff B (50%)
  ), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

  strict_results[[i]] <- sim.epi_seir(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, nSeeds = nSeeds,
    R0 = R0, t.stop = t.stop, roles = roles, 
    group_assign = scenario3, M = M_strict)
}



```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot of the incidence over time for 3 scenarios
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plotting a few summary measures
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)

total_cases <- sapply(baseline_results, function(x) sum(x$status.matrix$infected != 0))
w <- which.max(total_cases)

plot_data <- baseline_results[[w]]$sim.info
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = day, y = dailyInc)) +
  geom_line(color = "firebrick", size = 1) +
  geom_area(fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Daily Infection Incidence in Free Mixing network",
       x = "Day", y = "New Cases") +
  theme_minimal()


total_cases <- sapply(group_results, function(x) sum(x$status.matrix$infected != 0))
w <- which.max(total_cases)

plot_data <- group_results[[w]]$sim.info
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = day, y = dailyInc)) +
  geom_line(color = "firebrick", size = 1) +
  geom_area(fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Daily Infection Incidence in 2 Groups with Staff moving between",
       x = "Day", y = "New Cases") +
  theme_minimal()

total_cases <- sapply(strict_results, function(x) sum(x$status.matrix$infected != 0))
w <- which.max(total_cases)

plot_data <- strict_results[[w]]$sim.info
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = day, y = dailyInc)) +
  geom_line(color = "firebrick", size = 1) +
  geom_area(fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Daily Infection Incidence in Strict Cohorting",
       x = "Day", y = "New Cases") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot Attack rate for 3 scenarios
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Function to calculate metrics for a list of simulation results
get_metrics <- function(results_list, n, threshold = 0.10) {
  attack_rates <- sapply(results_list, function(res) {
    # Count individuals who were ever infected (status is not 0)
    sum(res$status.matrix$infected != 0) / n
  })
  
  # Define outbreaks below the threshold as "extinct"
  is_extinct <- attack_rates < threshold
  return(list(ar = attack_rates, extinct_rate = mean(is_extinct)))
}

# Calculate metrics for the 3 scenarios
m_baseline <- get_metrics(baseline_results, n)
m_group    <- get_metrics(group_results, n)
m_strict   <- get_metrics(strict_results, n)

# --- Plot Setup (3 columns for the 3 Scenarios) ---
par(mfrow=c(1, 3)) 

# Scenario 1: Baseline (Free mixing)
hist(m_baseline$ar, main="Scenario 1: Free mixing", 
     xlab="Attack Rate", col="skyblue", xlim=c(0,1), breaks=20)

# Scenario 2: Grouping (Two Groups with Staff)
hist(m_group$ar, main="Scenario 2: Two Groups with Staff", 
     xlab="Attack Rate", col="lightgreen", xlim=c(0,1), breaks=20)

# Scenario 3: Strict Network (Strict Groups)
hist(m_strict$ar, main="Scenario 3: Strict Groups", 
     xlab="Attack Rate", col="salmon", xlim=c(0,1), breaks=20)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot Outbreak Probability for 3 scenarios
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Set up side-by-side bar plots
par(mfrow=c(1, 3))

# Quick helper function for bar plots
plot_outcome <- function(m_data, title) {
  barplot(c(Extinct = m_data$extinct_rate, Major = 1 - m_data$extinct_rate), 
          main = title, col = c("grey", "orange"), ylab = "Probability", ylim=c(0,1))
}

# Generate plots for the 3 scenarios
plot_outcome(m_baseline, "Scenario 1: Free mixing")
plot_outcome(m_group, "Scenario 2: Two Groups with Staff")
plot_outcome(m_strict, "Scenario 3: Strict Groups")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot attack rate (non-extinct) for 3 scenarios
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Set layout to 1 row and 3 columns
par(mfrow=c(1, 3), mar=c(4.4, 4.1, 3.1, 1.1))

# List of results to iterate through
scenarios_list <- list(Baseline = baseline_results, 
                       Groups = group_results, 
                       Strict = strict_results)

# Colors for the 3 plots
colors <- c("skyblue", "lightgreen", "orange")

for(i in 1:length(scenarios_list)) {
  current_res <- scenarios_list[[i]]
  name <- names(scenarios_list)[i]
  
  # 1. Calculate Attack Rate for all nSim runs
  ar_all <- sapply(current_res, function(res) {
    sum(res$status.matrix$infected != 0) / n
  })
  
  # 2. Filter for Major outbreaks (Attack Rate >= 10%)
  major_ar <- ar_all[ar_all >= 0.10]
  
  # 3. Draw histogram
  if(length(major_ar) > 0) {
    hist(major_ar, 
         main = paste(name, ": Major AR"), 
         xlab = "Proportion Infected", 
         ylab = "Frequency",
         col  = colors[i], 
         xlim = c(0, 1),      # Fixed X-axis
         ylim = c(0, 100),    # Unified Y-axis set to 100
         breaks = seq(0, 1, by=0.1))
  } else {
    # Placeholder for scenarios with no major outbreaks
    plot(NULL, xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,100), 
         main = paste(name, ": No Major Outbreak"), 
         xlab = "Proportion Infected", ylab = "Frequency", axes = TRUE)
    text(0.5, 50, "0% Major Outbreaks", col = "red", cex = 1.2)
  }
}


```

```{r}
n<- 28 # population size
ct.rates<-3 # avg number of daily contacts per day
nSeeds<-1 # number of cases starting the epidemic
R0<-1.5 # average number of secondary cases generated per infected individual in a fully susceptible population
inf.param<- R0/(ct.rates)
# pathogen<-"COVID-19"

# Compute the reproduction number related to the selected network. 
source("F:\\Statistics UHasselt\\Semester 4\\Master Thesis\\Master-Thesis---Chau-\\SEIR.R")
nSim<-1000
nSeed<-01042026
set.seed(nSeed)

baseline_results <- list() 
group_results <- list() 
strict_results <- list()

for (i in 1:nSim) {
  if (i %% 100 == 0) {
    cat("Simulation:", i, "/", nSim, "\n")}
  
  # SCENARIO 1: Free mixing (baseline)
  baseline_results[[i]] <- sim.epi_seir(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, nSeeds = 1, inf.param = inf.param, t.stop = t.stop)
  
  # SCENARIO 2: Staff-Bridge - Volunteers in rooms + Staff moving between
  # IDs 1-12: Volunteers Group A | IDs 13-24: Volunteers Group B | IDs 25-28: Staff
  volunteers_a <- 12
  volunteers_b <- 12
  staff  <- 4
  
  scenario2 <- c(rep(1, volunteers_a), rep(2, volunteers_b), rep(3, staff))
  
  # Mixing Matrix (M) for 3 groups:
  # Rows = Infector Group, Cols = Potential Infectee Group
  # Probabilities should represent the likelihood of contact
  M_matrix <- matrix(c(
    0.90, 0.00, 0.10,  # Group 1 (Volunteers A) stays in Room A (90%), only sees Staff (10%)
    0.00, 0.90, 0.10,  # Group 2 (Volunteers B) stays in Room B (90%), only sees Staff (10%)
    0.40, 0.40, 0.20   # Group 3 (Staff) visits A (40%), B (40%), and other Staff (20%)
  ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)

  group_results[[i]] <- sim.epi_seir(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, 
    nSeeds = 1, 
    inf.param = inf.param, t.stop = t.stop, 
    group_assign = scenario2, M = M_matrix)

  # SCENARIO 3: Strict Cohorting - Staff A for Group A, Staff B for Group B
  # n=28: 12 Volunteers A, 12 Volunteers B, 2 Staff A, 2 Staff B
  volunteers_room <- 12
  staff_room <- 2
  
  # Group 1: Volunteers A | Group 2: Volunteers B | Group 3: Staff A | Group 4: Staff B
  scenario3 <- c(rep(1, volunteers_room), rep(2, volunteers_room), 
                     rep(3, staff_room), rep(4, staff_room))
  
  # Matrix M for 4 groups: Staff A (Group 3) only meets Volunteers A (Group 1). Staff B (Group 4) only meets Volunteers B (Group 2).
  # There is no overlap between Group (1,3) and Group (2,4).
  M_strict <- matrix(c(
    0.90, 0.00, 0.10, 0.00,  # Group 1 (Volunteers A) stays in Room A (90%), only sees Staff A (10%)
    0.00, 0.90, 0.00, 0.10,  # Group 2 (Volunteers B) stays in Room B (90%), only sees Staff B (10%)
    0.50, 0.00, 0.50, 0.00,  # Group 3 (Staff A) visits A (50%), and other Staff A (50%)
    0.00, 0.50, 0.00, 0.50   # Group 3 (Staff B) visits B (50%), and other Staff B (50%)
  ), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

  strict_results[[i]] <- sim.epi_seir(
    n = n, ct.rates = ct.rates, 
    nSeeds = 1,
    inf.param = inf.param, t.stop = t.stop, 
    group_assign = scenario3, M = M_strict)
}
```
